Command: Do Not Kill Mother and Young on the Same Day
Summary: And whether it be cow or ewe, ye shall not kill it and her young both in one day. This is distinct from the live Sacrifices row, whose Leviticus range ends at chapter 7.
Commandment: Do not kill a cow or ewe and her young both on one day.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as moral. The companion law is the mother bird (Deuteronomy 22:6-7, drafted separately): in both cases the next generation is not taken together with the parent. Mercy to animals is a thread of the Law, not an afterthought — the righteous man regards the life of his beast (Proverbs 12:10).
Purpose: TRADITIONAL reading: the pairing of mother and young on one day offends the compassion the Law elsewhere commands toward animals; Scripture states the prohibition without a reason (Leviticus 22:28).
